mock_response.reasoning: Matches this vendor's default account exactly.

note: Deliberately constructed gap case: this specific invoice from an otherwise-reliable vendor was actually a genuine one-off exception (e.g. a different type of purchase from the same supplier) that needed a different account. Nothing available to the system -- not the vendor's default, not the model's confidence -- signals that anything is unusual, so every check passes and the entry auto-approves. It is, in fact, wrong. This is what evaluation.md's inappropriate_automation_rate metric exists to surface: the residual risk that remains even after every documented control passes.
